feature: Type a number into a slider
summary: Every number in the Effects list and in Appearance is now a box you can type an exact number into, instead of a knob you nudge until the readout agrees. A border 12 wide, a glow 30 soft, a line exactly 2 points thick on a 24 pixel icon: type it and press return.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing to switch on.

try.do: Draw a rectangle, then add a Border from the Effects list.
Click the number beside Width, type 12, press Return.
Click the number beside Offset, type 99, press Return. It stops at 40, the end of the slider.
Press Command Z once. The offset goes back, in one step, and the width is untouched.
Click into Offset, type the word wide, press Return. The old number comes back.
With the keyboard still in a number, press Up and Down, then Shift Up.
Draw an arrow and type 9 into Thickness and 2.5 into Head Size, in Appearance.
Pick two rectangles with different borders. The box says Mixed; type a number and both take it.

evaluate: Does clicking the number feel like the obvious way to set an exact one, or did you still reach for the knob first?

The box is 8 points taller than the plain number it replaced, so a layer wearing a shadow, a border and a glow is about 90 points taller in the panel than it was. Is that a fair price, or does the Effects list now feel too long to scroll?
Is a box on every row too much box? Would you rather it looked like plain text until you clicked it?
The unit word moved out of the number and sits beside the box, so it reads 12 px as two pieces rather than one. Does that still read as one number?
Head Size shows a multiple with its sign in front, as ×2.5. Is that the number you would think to type?
rough: NO PICTURES IN THIS AUDIT. The Mac's screen was locked for the whole of this task, so macOS never drew the app and no walk could run: this feature has not been seen working, only built and reasoned about. The walk that proves it is written and committed (Scripts/playtest/type-into-an-effects-slider-walk.json) and a full sweep has been asked for, so the first sweep after the screen is unlocked either confirms it or files what it found.

The panel got taller. Measured with real control metrics: a slider row goes from 29 points to 37. I tried putting the box at the end of the slider's own track instead, which saves exactly one point, and putting the name, the slider and the box all on one line, which saves eight but leaves the slider about 70 points of track in a 264 point panel. Neither was worth it, so the box sits where the readout sat and the row is taller.

Three numbers in the panel still cannot be typed: a shape's Corner Radius, a measurement's Chip size, and the Width slider in the older shape controls. Corner Radius was left out on purpose rather than forgotten, because it has a floor that refuses part of the range and an answer line that explains a refused drag, and whether a typed number below that floor should raise the same answer is a question worth deciding rather than guessing. Filed as its own task.
Label corners keeps its plain readout, because its answer is a word at both ends (Square, Pill) and there is nothing to type.

Two panels were quietly writing lengths in "pt" while the rest of the app says "px": the effect styles editor and a motion row for stroke width. Both say the app's one word now. That was not asked for; it was in the way.
